failures.claim: The organisation uses external physical risk exposure information as an input to its climate-related risk processes, including ECB climate indicators, alongside internal risk documentation in the climate risk register.

Risk ratings in the climate risk register are derived from a 5x5 risk matrix using the formula likelihood_score * severity_score, with thresholds: 1–2 low, 3–6 medium, 8–12 high, 15–25 critical (equivalently critical >= 15, high >= 8, medium >= 3, low < 3).
The climate risk register includes risks rated "medium".

The climate risk register includes an indicator of whether a risk has changed since the prior reporting period, and some climate-related risks have changed since the prior reporting period while others have not.
Climate-related risks identified for operational activities include that operational sites and travel generate Scope 1–2 emissions and face physical disruption.
Climate-related risks identified in relation to lending include that lending to Other mining and quarrying carries elevated transition risk from carbon pricing and demand shifts.

Consistent with an integrated approach, climate-related risks are documented, assessed and monitored through the same core risk artefact (the climate risk register), supporting coherent risk management disclosure without unnecessary duplication.
